Taiwan and Korea quiet: no GPS jamming or internet disruption.

categories.summary: All Australian carriers normal and the global threat level is green. Two foreign-flagged vessels loitered near the Sunshine Coast cable landing this morning; no damage reported. Overseas: IT firm N-able took its platform offline after 30+ zero-days were published, and an AI-driven attack on a European telco was reported. Australian breaches remain data-theft, not outages. ACSC feed timed out.

categories.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has passed 10,600 cases with imported cases in Kenya and Nigeria. Serious but distant; risk to SA limited to rare imported cases. The collector's 'mystery pneumonia' and chemical matches are old or unrelated stories; the pandemic-stock rise is led by Moderna and Novavax.

headline: Watch: Hormuz shipping disruption keeps fuel the main risk for SA; this morning's cable-vessel alerts were not confirmed as anything harmful.
summary: Little change since this morning. US-Iran talks over Hormuz remain unresolved, but oil eased again to about US$91.50 and the market fear index fell back below 20. Two Chinese/Hong Kong-flagged vessels slowed near the Sunshine Coast cable landing this morning; no cable damage or outage has been reported and all Australian phone and internet networks are normal. No SA weather emergencies.
